source.anchor_kjv: And they brought young children to him, that he should touch them: and his disciples rebuked those that brought them. But when Jesus saw it, he was much displeased, and said unto them, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God. Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein. And he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them.
source.hook_line: NARRATOR: Has someone pushed you away? Told you "not now"? This story is for you.
source.spoken_script: NARRATOR: Has someone pushed you away? Told you "not now"? This story is for you. People were bringing young children to Jesus. They wanted one thing: "that he should touch them." But His own close followers "rebuked those that brought them." They tried to stop them. Then Jesus saw it. And the Bible says He was "much displeased." Angry. Not with the children. With the ones who tried to stop them. JESUS: "Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God." NARRATOR: In plain words: let them come. Do not stop them. God's kingdom belongs to people like these children. And grown-ups must receive it the same way: like a little child. And here is what He did. "He took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them." The people came for a touch. He gave the children His arms. Someone told you "not now." Look at who Jesus picked up.

platforms.title: Let the Children Come to Me: Why Jesus Got Angry | Bible Story
platforms.description:
Jesus and the little children in the Bible (Mark 10:13-16): His own followers tried to stop people bringing children to Him, and Jesus was angry.

"Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God." In old English, "suffer" means "let". In plain words: let the children come, do not stop them. The kingdom of God belongs to people like them.

The Bible's words are "much displeased". In one plain word: angry. Not with the children. With the ones who tried to stop them.

He also said: "Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein." Grown-ups come to God the same way: like a little child.

"Not now" in the film is our short way to say it. It is not a Bible quote. The Bible says the followers "rebuked those that brought them."

Has someone told you "not now"? Jesus did not send those children away. You can come to Him too.

Read it: Mark 10:13-16 (also Matthew 19:13-15, Luke 18:15-17).

redteam:
VERDICT: REVISE
- All platforms: "Jesus was angry" rests on KJV "much displeased" (Mark 10:14). Defensible, and the YouTube description ties the two words together, but TikTok and Instagram say "angry" with no link to "much displeased". Fix: keep, but the external panel should check it.
- youtube_short title "Why Jesus Got Angry": the video answers the why (they tried to stop the children), so it is honest; check it does not read as Jesus losing His temper.
- All platforms: "Jesus' own followers tried to stop ..." is the narration's plain gloss of "rebuked those that brought them"; the KJV does not say "stop". Acceptable as a plain gloss; it is beside the real quote on YouTube and Facebook.
- "Grown-ups come to God the same way: like a little child" softens Mark 10:15's "shall not enter therein"; the verse is quoted in full just before it, so no doctrine is hidden.
- Quoted KJV fragments checked against the anchor: verbatim.
- Run the external blind panel on this copy before calling it final.
